elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 15.5 is untouched and reads "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York without reference to any rules of conflict of laws." New York is the preferred governing law, so no edit was required.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Revised 15.6(a) does designate "the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York," but the rendered document still retains operative arbitration machinery: "The language of the arbitration shall be English. The proceedings and decisions of the arbitrator shall be final and binding on the Parties, and judgment on the award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction," plus the surviving JAMS Expedited Procedures modifications. A binding-arbitral-award sentence sitting alongside an exclusive-court clause is internally inconsistent, and the drafter only promises in the margin comment that 15.6(b)-(g) "should be struck in the conforming pass" rather than striking them in the operative language. Separately, the retained carve-out in 15.6(j) permits either Party to seek "equitable relief" generally from "a court of competent jurisdiction" and is temporally anchored to "prior to or during any arbitration" \u2014 broader than temporary injunctive relief and now anchored to a proceeding the redline eliminates.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The clause retains New York law (Section 15.5) and the redline makes no change to governing law. New York is the preferred, not the fallback, law, so the fallback law element is literally unsatisfied; the fallback level is not the level being pursued.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The redline designates New York County state and federal courts; no Delaware, California, or London forum appears anywhere in the rendered language.

reasons: Preferred forum element fails on internal inconsistency: the rendered text still contains "The proceedings and decisions of the arbitrator shall be final and binding on the Parties, and judgment on the award may be entered in any court having jurisdiction" and the JAMS Expedited Procedures modifications, which directly contradict the new exclusive-court submission in 15.6(a). Repair: delete the residual arbitration provisions (the p0630 fragment and Sections 15.6(b)-(g)) in the operative redline rather than deferring them to a "conforming pass" \u2014 a promise in the margin comment does not count.

The retained 15.6(j) carve-out is now both broader than the element allows and dangling. It permits "equitable relief" from any "court of competent jurisdiction" (not solely temporary/interim injunctive relief) and is anchored "prior to or during any arbitration," a proceeding the redline removes. Repair: conform 15.6(j) to preserve only temporary restraining orders, preliminary injunctions, and other interim equitable relief, and delete the "prior to or during any arbitration" anchor (or replace it with "pending resolution of a Dispute in the courts designated in Section 15.6(a)").
Preferred element 1 is already satisfied by unmodified Section 15.5 (New York law), so no governing-law edit was needed and none was made \u2014 correct.

Fallback level is not pursued and is not met (law remains New York; no Delaware/California/London forum designated). That is acceptable only if the preferred level is completed, which it currently is not.

Minimality holds on what was changed: the edit is confined to the 15.6(a) referral sentence and the conforming "scope or applicability of this Section 15.6" tweak, with no added survival tails, expense language, or procedures. The defect is under-editing, not over-editing.

Intent fails because the redline leaves a contradictory retained sentence (binding arbitral award), orphaned JAMS procedural text with no operative arbitration referral, and a cross-reference in 15.6(j) to an arbitration that no longer exists.
